newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay's five-day rally gains strength, up one pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay's five-day rally gains strength, up one pct.

text.p: A flurry of buy orders by foreign funds in front-bencher scrips helped Bombay stocks on Tuesday to stage a powerful rally just before the close of trade and finish with sharp gains, dealers said.
"The market seems to be going up, up and away..we are seeing a bull run," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.

Marketmen said hectic buying by foreign funds in stocks such as cement giant ACC, bell-wether Reliance Industries and tobacco conglomerate ITC fuelled a sharp rise in prices. The rally spurred the Bombay index to a sixth consecutive higher close, a rise of 235 points or over seven percent.
"There's renewed interest...retail investors are also picking up mid-cap stocks," said a local dealer.
Indian stocks facing a loss of confidence from investors have raced ahead in the New Year boosted by government promises of policy measures to bolster industrial growth and revive sluggish markets.
The sharp rally had led some investors and fence-sitters to jump on the buying bandwagon, analysts said.
Ashish Kacholia, head of research at Prime Broking said the rally caused a change in investor sentiment, stoking appetites for small stocks.
"Investors are cautious buyers...they are looking at good quality stocks."
Traders said an early bout of cautiousness forced the market to fall in mid-session but buying by foreign funds helped the index to close higher.
The Bombay 30-share index ended 34.28 points higher at 3,487.44, up from it's intra-day low of 3,222.99.
ACC rose 109.0 rupees to 1,470.0 rupees, SBI 13.20 to 267.0, TISCO 5.25 to 194.25, ITC 18.0 to 381.0, BSES 19.0 to 246.75, Tata Power 7.0 to 141.50, L&T 5.0 to 249.75.
